editorial:
Imagine marrying someone not because you love them, but because they are a great tool to help you get ahead in your career. That is exactly what Lucas Marsh does. He is a driven medical student who wants to be the best doctor in the world, and he views Kristina as the perfect partner because she has money and knows how to run an operating room. You get to watch their relationship start as a calculated business move, with Kristina being the sweet, supportive wife who puts her own needs last. The vibe is heavy on old-school drama, showing the dark side of ambition and how cold a person can be when they only care about success.

You will find that the acting is top-notch, especially seeing the slow break in Kristina's spirit as Lucas starts cheating on her with a local woman. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow by today's standards. If you enjoy stories about betrayal and moral lessons, you will love this. Since this is a classic, you should look for the best version possible.
endingExplained: The movie ends in a tragic way. After Lucas treats Kristina poorly for years, he finally realizes he loves her, but it is too late. Kristina gets sick and eventually dies. In her final moments, she forgives him, which makes the guilt even worse for Lucas. He ends up successful in his career, but he is completely alone and broken, realizing that his ambition cost him the only person who actually cared for him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood dramas about marriage and regret.
